page.layout: Two coin engravings side by side at the top, with no text block between them and the text. Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs. Signature "Kk 2" at the lower right under the text. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: ALEXANDER, cognominatus magnus, successit patri Philippo in regno Macedoniæ, anno mundi 3 6 2 8. ante Christum natum 334. anno ætatis 20:hic conspecta Asia, summo desiderio obtinendę accensus, ac spe eximia, patrimonium omne suum quod in Macedonia Europaque habebat, amicis diuidit, sibi Asiam sufficere præfatus. Persis dictitans longa iam satis & matura imperia contigisse, quorumque tepus esset vices excipere melius acturos. Sed neque alia quàm regis animorum, exercitus præsumptio fuit: nam obliti omnes coniugum liberorumque, & longinquæ à domo militiæ, Persicum aurum, & totius orientis opes, iam quasi suam prædā ducebāt, nec belli periculorum, sed diuitiarum meminerant. milites à populatione Asiæ prohibuit, parcedum suis rebus præfatus, nec perdenda ea quæ possessuri venerant. In exercitu habuit peditum 3 2 0 0 0. equitum 4500. naues 182. Milites elegit veteranos, vt magistros militiæ magis quàm milites electos putares. Dariū vicit. Persarum peditum 2 0 0 0 0. occidit: equitum 1 5 0 0. mater, vxor, filiæ Darij captæ sunt. Babyloniā cepit, Persepolim diripuit, Indiam ad Gangem vsque obtinuit. Imperauit annos 12. Vide Plutar. in eius vita, & Iusti. multis in locis.
THALESTRIS, Amazonum regina, Alexandrum adiit, concubitum ad prolem suscipiendam petiit, & obtinuit. Vide Iusti.li. 2. & 12. Quin.Cur.lib.6. Oro.li.3.ca.18. de hac vide etiam supra in Penthesilea.

page.notes: Two coin engravings above the text, not transcribed as text. Left coin: legend "ALEXANDER" around the rim, with "M." at the top. Right coin: legend "THALESTRIA" down the right rim, and the left rim legend is only partly legible ("AMAZ..." / "REG..."), so I have not transcribed it. The "Kk 2" signature is read with some doubt. The numbers are copied as printed, with the spaced digits of the original. Tepus (for tempus) and Dariū are printing forms and are left as printed.
